pageCache.text:
A warm welcome from our Headteacher
On behalf of the pupils, staff, parents and governors, I am delighted to welcome you to Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School’s website.
Our school is a small, caring and happy one where all the children and teachers know one another and where every child matters. We have high standards of academic achievement, with Key Stage figures consistently above both national. However, our school is about so much more than just results.
What's going on Day to day life at school
"As part of our current RE topic, Creation and Covenant, Year 4 narrated the story of Abraham using improvisation to act and react to the events in Scripture. Following the drama activity, the children discussed how Abraham's faith and trust in God influenced each of his decisions!" ~ Mrs Furrer #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"This half term in Geography, the children in Years 1 and 2 have been learning about seas and coasts. They have been exploring the seven continents and five oceans of the world and developing their map-reading skills. The children became mini explorers and located different countries and identified which continent they belong to!" ~ Mrs Harvey & Miss Wilding #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"PE has got off to a good start in Year 5! We have been testing our fitness levels and have learnt the six elements of fitness we will be focusing on this half term: Strength, Speed, Stamina, Co-Ordination, Agility and Flexibility. During this lesson, the children were asked to skip for a minute, counting how many they completed, take a break and do it again to try and beat their scores. This required co-ordination but also speed. The children also tried to 'Beat the Ball' before it was passed to the final person; testing out our agility, speed, and stamina . A very competitive lesson but a fun one all the same!" ~ Miss O'Brien #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"It was fantastic to see our netball team out bright and early before school, practising their drills! They all showed great enthusiasm and team team spirit. Well done, team!" ~ Mrs Orchard #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"In English, we have been reading the first part of Treason. We have been discussing how Will and Margery would have felt about Matthew's death, and also Father deciding to leave them behind (with Aunt Carew) to go and work with Lord Carew in London. We created our own freeze frames to display our emotions regarding the situation, and write about what we predict will happen next now that Aunt Carew is coming to stay. We're looking forward to seeing what happens!" ~ Miss O'Brien #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"In RE, Year 6 enjoyed dramatising different parts of the second story of creation from the book of Genesis! They chose a key word and acted out the part of the story that they felt was best suited to that word: blame, responsibility, deceit, dishonesty and vulnerability." ~ Mrs Saulet #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"In RE, Year 1 have been learning about the Creation Story. The children spent time outside listening, feeling and looking closely at the little details around them, then shared what they noticed and wondered about the world God created. Finally, they collaborated on a chalk mind-map of the natural beauty in their very own playground!" ~ Miss Wilding #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"Year 4 have been having lots of fun investigating the place value of numbers up to 10,000! They worked together to order numbers in ascending and descending order, explaining their reasoning and why each number belonged in its particular place. Great teamwork and mathematical thinking!" ~ Mrs Furrer #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"In RE, Year 5 have been learning about covenants as part of our 'Creation and Covenant' topic! We role-played the covenant Moses made with God and the story of him receiving the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai. The children thought carefully about how they would have been feeling as their characters, and decided whether the Ten Commandments were restrictive, or if they promoted freedom." ~ Miss O'Brien #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"Year 4 have been investigating the differences between solids and liquids in Science. As part of our practical work, we have investigated three different materials, ketchup, toothpaste and oobleck, which act like solids or liquids (non-Newtonian fluid) according to the force acting on them. We found out that you could pick oobleck up, and roll it into a ball before letting it ooze out between our fingers. We had a lot of fun working together to investigate these materials!" ~ Mrs Furrer #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"Year 2's first PE topic is gymnastics. The children were exploring and performing different shapes they can make with their bodies. With the expert guidance of Mrs Dobson, they developed their confidence by linking the shapes together to make a sequence!" ~ Mrs Harvey #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"Year 2 have enjoyed their first week back at school and have got off to a great start! They had lots of fun playing parachute games in PE, developing their teamwork and communication skills while working together. Well done, Year 2!" ~ Mrs Harvey #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"Year 1 have been enjoying playing a variety of maths games as part of their maths lessons! The children have been doing a great job supporting and helping each other to play the games correctly." ~ Miss Wilding #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill
"Year 2 are back and enjoying their Mastering Number lessons. Here they are using their Rekenreks - these counting frames are used in early maths education to help the children develop number sense, understand place value and visualise addition and subtraction. Well done Year 2 and Mrs Harvey!" ~ Mrs Green #SacredHeart #Teddington #HamptonWick #Kingston #Twickenham #HamptonHill #Hampton #StrawberryHill

Personally, I would definitely say that one of the things Sacred Heart is great at is looking out and helping the individual pupil. The staff also are great influences on the children – everybody shows the school’s values.
Sacred Heart School goes above and beyond in addressing children's needs and nurturing their unique talents. Thanks to their exceptional, personalised approach and welcoming atmosphere, children are flourishing.
The teachers always paid attention to everyone's learning. For instance, some children and I would have a higher level of a certain subject taught to us.
The school is ready to help pupils whenever needed. They have different ways of boosting our learning, not just ordinary work and they try to find ways to make it fun.
When I joined this amazing school - Sacred Heart - I started in Year 3, I had no idea how to read or write. However, the teachers helped me achieve my goals by supporting me every step of the way.
I have learnt that I can do anything when I put my mind to it.
I have improved my ability and attitude towards my learning and towards making friends as I am quiet in nature. Now I have more confidence.
As Sacred Heart School itself is a small school, you know all the teachers and students, so when you walk into the corridor in the morning you always have a friendly face to greet you.
The strengths of Sacred Heart are how resilient the teachers and other support staff make us feel.
I have developed much better skills in all subjects and my achievements are playing for the football team and getting a main part in the production.
The school has introduced many more clubs and pupil groups for lots of people to join.

This the second ungraded inspection since the school was judge to be good in March 2017. These are carried out by an HM Inspector with the intention of validating that a school remains a ‘Good’ school. The foci of this type of inspection are:
The outcome of this inspection is that Sacred Heart remains a ‘Good‘ school.
The report can be read using the link below.

quality of education
behaviour and attitudes
personal development

Catholic School Inspection

Catholic Social Teaching
Catholic Social Teaching
At Sacred Heart, through our Catholic Social Teaching, we aim to support our children in the development of moral character, a sense of social responsibility, and an understanding of the importance of helping those in need. We aim to instil values like kindness, justice, and respect for others, fostering a foundation for ethical decision-making and compassionate engagement with the community.
Catholic Social Teaching is based on the belief that God has a plan for creation, a plan to build his kingdom of peace, love and justice.
It holds that God has a special plan for every single one of us, whoever we are. Our part in this plan isn’t just limited to things ‘spiritual’, or times when we do “religious things.” It involves every aspect of our lives, from the things we pray about, to how we live as a responsible global citizen.
Our part in this story is a kind-of vocation for the common good, a call to treat everyone as our brothers and sisters. It is something that we all share.
The Catholic Church has seven principles of social teaching that we share with our children through all that we do, through the curriculum, special events and activities, and through our ordinary actions in school.
At Sacred Heart, Catholic Social Teaching is incorporated into our curriculum. Children are asked to put their faith into action and reflect on how their learning enables them to do so. We also reflect on these during Collective Worships.
Catholic Social Teaching underpins the essence of our daily school life. As members of the Catholic Church, we are all called upon to preserve the dignity of all human beings, to care for creation, and to reach out to our sisters and brothers in need. Pope Francis, when he was alive, emphasised that it is our duty to work together to bring about a more just and peaceful world: to put love into action. It is vital that our children can articulate the connection between Jesus' teaching and doing good deeds.
We use the Caritas, 'Rooted in Love' and CAFOD Catholic Social Teaching resources to support the children’s understanding of principles. All our Year 5 pupils undertake the Caritas Ambassador Programme with the goal of them becoming leaders in social action at school and sharing what they have learnt with those around them.
We are called to uphold the principles of Catholic Social Teaching.
Human Dignity – Everyone is Special
St Paul tells us that each person is a work of art, created by God and chosen for a unique purpose. Ephesians 2:10
At Sacred Heart we recognise the human dignity of others by:
being respectful
treating people equally
raising awareness of civil rights
preferential option for the vulnerable
The Common Good– Taking part in our Communities
"You are not making a gift of your possessions to the poor person. You are handing over to them what is theirs." St Ambrose (340-397 AD)
At Sacred Heart we show we are part of a community by:
working together
working for the common good
participating and engaging
being active members of our community
Participation – The dignity of Work
Do the hard work of getting along with each other, treating each other with dignity and honour. (James 3:17)
And he said to him, “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind. This is the great and first commandment. And a second is like it: You shall love your neighbour as yourself. On these two commandments depends all the Law and the Prophets.” Matthew 22:37-40
At Sacred Heart we recognise the dignity of work by:
respecting all workers
contributing to society
making responsible economic choices
supporting wellbeing and workers' rights
sharing our talents with others
Subsidiarity– All people should have a say
Blessed are they who maintain justice, who constantly do what is right- Psalm 106:3
Fear not for I am with you. I am your God. I will strengthen you. I will help you. I will uphold you with my righteous right hand. Isaiah 41:10
At Sacred Heart we acknowledge our rights and responsibilities by:
standing up for what is right
following our school rules
Stewardship – Caring for God’s Creation and Gifts
The ecological crisis is also a summons to profound interior conversion…Living our vocation to be protectors of God’s handiwork is essential to a life of virtue; it is not an optional or a secondary aspect of our Christian experience. Pope Francis - Laudato Si
At Sacred Heart we show we care for creation by:
taking responsibility for our environment
making environmentally responsible choices
Solidarity – We are One Big Family
Blessed Pope Paul VI taught that "If you want peace, work for justice". The Gospel calls us to be peacemakers.
At Sacred Heart we show solidarity by:
raising awareness of social justice
writing to our local leaders
praying for others
making connections
making socially responsible choices
Option for the poor – Some People need Extra Help
‘For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in, I needed clothes and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to visit me.’ Matthew 25:35-40
At Sacred Heart we show a preferential option for the poor and vulnerable by:
fundraising for charitable causes
raising awareness
treating others with dignity and respect
thinking of the needs of others
Distributive Justice – Being Fair
...'we are agreed today that the earth is essentially a shared inheritance, whose fruits are meant to benefit everyone.’ Pope Francis, Laudato Si’
At Sacred Heart we recognise the need to share the world's resources fairly by:
becoming Fair Trade aware as a school
trying to buy Fair Trade
by sharing our belongings
Promoting Peace – We can be God’s instruments of Peace
“Our common bonds of humanity demand that we live in harmony and that we promote what is good for one another. These ethical implications are the reason why solidarity is a basic key to peace.” St John Paul II
At Sacred Heart we show we are people of peace by:
treating each other kindly
turning away from conflict
creating bonds between people

pageCache.text:
Church Ministries
Our pupils are encouraged to help out with ministries in their local parish.
Ministers of the Word
In proclaiming the word of God, readers exercise their responsibility in mediating the presence of Christ. God speaks to the congregation through them, and, the impact of God’s message will depend significantly on their conviction, their preparation, and their delivery.
The reader has responsibility for not simply reading the word, but assisting the congregation to hear the word. This requires the reader to be attentive to the congregation, and careful to allow for times of pause and silence as the congregation prepares to listen and, once the reading has been proclaimed, as it takes the word of God to heart.
We are incredibly lucky to have a team of readers from Sacred Heart School who help us understand the ‘Liturgy of the Word’ each week. We thank them for their service and commitment to this role – it can be very difficult to read and project your voice to a church full of people.
Welcome Team
A servant's heart is the most important quality when practising this ministry. This team is made up of families who share their warmth and hospitality by giving a friendly smile to make people feel welcome at Sacred Heart Church.
Whoever you are, wherever you are from, whatever your background, you are welcome at Sacred Heart and the welcome team serve others by ensuring the congregation have the books and information needed to participate and share in the Mass with our whole congregation. They also hand out the parish newsletter.
Thank you to the children from Sacred Heart and their families for carrying out this incredibly important ministry. You are the first people visitors see and you give that first impression of what our community is like – a happy place to be, a place where we can come to know God more closely.
Altar Server's Ministry
A number of our pupils are Altar Servers or are in training to be Altar Servers. Our Altar Servers enjoy serving Mass in school and in the parish.
Thank you all for your service.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School & Nursery - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Welcome from our Headteacher - Mrs Green
On behalf of the pupils, staff, parents and governors, I am delighted to welcome you to Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School.
At Sacred Heart, children ‘Grow in Love’. All the children and teachers know one another and every individual child’s own learning and development matter deeply to us.
Our Key Stage figures are consistently well above the national average, however, our school is about so much more than just results.
Everything we do is underpinned by our values of Achievement, Care, Consideration, Generosity, Love, Mutual Respect, Patience, Prayer and Tolerance.
We support children to develop, academically, mentally, physically and spiritually and work closely with our local Church, Sacred Heart. As a Catholic school, we welcome families of all faiths and none and we are proud of the multicultural, multispirtual heritage of our community. As one parent described it, 'Sacred Heart is like a mini-world in a playground’.
We have a broad and creative curriculum that challenges and develops the individual child, helping them to explore their interests and abilities.
Our children enjoy access to excellent music and sporting facilities and make the most of our extensive playing field and outdoor spaces.
We provide support for busy working parents and carers with our selection of popular after-school clubs including cookery, gardening, sewing, art, dance, drama, chess, tennis, football, gymnastics, multi-sports and running. We also have our own on-site Breakfast Club and After-School Club offering child care from 7.30 am to 6.15 pm each weekday.
Our school is a place where children have their say in how things run. Through elected School Councillors and pupil groups such as the Eco Team and Young Interpreters, our students' voices are heard.
Children enjoy that there is lots of integration amongst the different age groups with buddy-systems, whole school assemblies and Do Something Different Days which connect the Infants and Juniors.
We have partnerships with local churches, colleges and schools and have many visitors to Sacred Heart who enrich our children’s education. A thriving Parent Teacher Association ensures lots of well-supported fundraising events throughout the year, and many of our parents help in the classroom, behind the scenes and on school trips.
Our aim is to work with you to provide your children with the best possible start in life, developing children who are confident, caring, responsible and independent. If you would like to see us in action, we would be delighted to show you around our school – simply call our school office to make an appointment.

Information for Prospective Parents & School Tours
Welcome to Sacred Heart Primary School Teddington
Welcome to Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School
Sacred Heart School is a wonderfully-unique, one-form entry Catholic Primary school in the heart of Teddington.
We serve all the Catholic parishes in the area and also welcome families of other faiths and none.
We would be delighted to show you around our school. We have 30 places in Reception and 26 places in our Nursery. We also have a few vacancies in specific year groups if you have older children who require an in-year school place.
Please call the school office on 020 8977 6591. If you are new to the area and require a school place outside of the normal admission's cycle, then please mention this when you call and we will arrange a convenient time to visit. For admission arrangements, please visit our Admissions Page.
Reception Tours for September 2027 Entry
We would love to welcome you to our Reception! From Tuesday 22nd September 2026, tours will be held every Tuesday morning at 9.40 am for September 2027 entry. Tours usually last around an hour.
If you cannot make a Tuesday tour, please call the school office and we will endeavour to fit you in on an alternative day. Please let the school office know if you would like to join us — we look forward to meeting you!
Call 0208 977 6591 or email info@sacredheart.richmond.sch.uk to book your place.

pageCache.pageTitle: Sacred Heart Catholic Primary School & Nursery - Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Curriculum at Sacred Heart
At Sacred Heart, we work to fulfil the vision that each pupil will:
demonstrate our school values and be active contributors at school, home and in the wider society
value and develop their unique talents and gifts to reach their full academic and spiritual potential
be effective communicators
be aspirational for themselves and their peers
develop their skills, knowledge and understanding to thrive as life-long learners
In order to achieve this, we follow the Early Years Foundation Stage and teach the National Curriculum. This is to ensure children have the knowledge and skills needed year-on-year to ensure good progress throughout their primary school education. We have designed our curriculum with additional experiences and enrichment activities to help children learn more and remember more.
RE is a core subject at Sacred Heart and is based on the Curriculum Directory (guidance from the Bishops of England and Wales) detailing what should be taught in each phase throughout the school. RE permeates all aspects of school life. Within RE we teach the children about all the major world religions and are always mindful that we have children of other faiths and no faith at school.
In addition to the Early Years Foundation Stage, National Curriculum and RE Curriculum, we overlay an additional focus on the Personal, Social and Emotional development of the individual. As a result, we adopt a relational approach to learning, which brings together the following inter-related curriculums and values:
We have a ThriveR accreditation and we are an ‘Attachment Aware’ school.
As a school, we believe the combination of the academic, relational curriculums and values-based approach, offer our pupils the best provision, enabling them to reach their full potential academically, personally, socially, emotionally and spiritually - ready for the next phase of their education and to achieve our mission to

SEND/Inclusion
SEND
This information relates to Special Educational Needs and Disability (SEND). You can follow the link to the Local Authorities Local Offer page, and have access to the school’s own ‘SEND Information for Parents’ document which outlines what parents can expect at Sacred Heart school.
The school's SEND and Inclusion Lead is Mrs Clare Taylor (Deputy Headteacher)
What is the Local Offer?
The Children and Families Bill was enacted in September 2014. From this date Local Authorities (LA) and schools are required to publish and keep under review information about services they expect to be available for children and young people with special educational needs (SEN) aged 0-25. The LA refer to this as the ‘Local Offer’.
The intention of the Local Offer is to improve choice and transparency for families. It will also be an important resource for parents in understanding the range of services and provision in the local area.
What is the Special Education Needs Information Report?
Schools utilise the LA Local Offer to meet the needs of SEND pupils as determined by school policy and the provision that the school is able to provide. Schools refer to this as ‘The Special Education Needs Information Report’.
Our SEND Inclusion Policy and the SEND Information Report have been ratified at the first Full Governing Body Meeting in Autumn term each year and can be accessed below and in the Policies section of the website.
